headline: Recycling transforms waste into raw materials—what was finished becomes a new beginning
universal_truth: Endings can become beginnings; what seems finished can be the start of something new
fun_facts: Aluminum can be recycled infinitely without losing quality—the same atoms keep cycling
Recycling one ton of paper saves 17 trees and 7,000 gallons of water
Glass takes over 1 million years to decompose but can be recycled endlessly
discussion_questions: What in your life could be 'recycled' into something new?
When have endings become new beginnings for you?
What old materials—skills, experiences, relationships—could serve new purposes?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Yesterday's newspaper becomes today's box. Old bottles become new containers. Recycling isn't just waste management—it's transformation. What was finished becomes raw material for something new. Endings become beginnings.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Recycling seems like just sorting trash. But there's a deeper principle about endings and new beginnings. What does transformation teach us?

options.text: Value doesn't disappear at endings—the materials persist even when the form is finished; transformation can recover value and create new purpose from old substance
options.response: Yes. The aluminum in a can is still aluminum. The paper's fibers are still fibers. Endings are about form, not substance. Value can be recovered through transformation.
It does reduce waste, but the principle extends beyond—transformation recovers value...

q1.title: Form vs Substance
q1.script: A can ends, aluminum continues. Form is temporary; substance persists. Recycling separates the two, recovering what lasts. The same principle applies beyond materials.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Form vs Substance"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Processing Required
q2.script: Transformation takes work—sorting, melting, reforming. Raw materials don't automatically become new things. Processing is required between endings and beginnings.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Personal Recycling
q3.script: You can recycle too—old skills in new careers, failed projects into learning, ended relationships into wisdom. The substance of your experience can be transformed into new forms.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Endings can become beginnings. What seems finished can be the start of something new. Transform rather than discard.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 281. Tomorrow, we'll explore food becoming soil—composting. Until then, consider what you could transform rather than discard.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Transformation Inventory - What Can Be Recycled?
growTrack.learning_objective: Identify opportunities for transformation rather than disposal
growTrack.activity: What in your life is 'finished' but still contains value? Old skills, past experiences, ended projects, former relationships? How could the substance be transformed into new forms? Endings are just material for new beginnings.
